dossier.public_summary: The 0.67-day dip coincides exactly with the star's 0.668-day spot rotation and shows a millimagnitude spot signal almost as large as the dip itself. The dip depth swings from ~14,000 ppm to ~1,800 ppm between sectors and individual transits scatter wildly, not behaving like a stable planet transit. The duration is too long for the M-dwarf density, favoring spots/variability on the target over a planet.

reasons.why: Period is exactly the stellar rotation period with millimagnitude spot amplitude comparable to the 7265 ppm dip; large out-of-eclipse swing at the same period with high chi2 indicates spots/variability at the transit period, not a planet.
reasons.value: rotation_d=0.668 vs signal_period_d=0.667792, signal_over_rotation=0.999688622754491, amplitude_ppm=37396, phase_curve amplitude_ppm=5863 ratio_to_depth=0.807 chi2=664.9 dof=7

reasons.why: Depth changes by a factor ~2 within the same SPOC source (p_constant 1.438098982277651e-10) and factor ~8 overall, inconsistent with a stable planet/detector calibration; sector 107 depth 1838±498 ppm disappears.
reasons.value: 1.574e-66, depth_change_pct=144.6, sector_depths_by_source verdict=changes_within_a_source, per-sector 14036,14429 ppm vs 7192,7490,7262,1838 ppm

reasons.why: Individual transits have huge scatter, formally inconsistent, showing the dip is not a repeatable transit shape.

Duration is far too long for a central planet on the measured M-dwarf and the density penalty is huge, matching an evolved-flat-bottom blend/eclipse more than a planet despite flat bottom v_sigma -3.597. Centroid on_target with xgboost planet_rank 0.11 supports stellar-variability/blend interpretation.
